rationale: One introduced defect blocks: exportChat builds the download filename identically with and without includeToolOutputs, so the two variants of the same conversation/format are indistinguishable on disk (CR-001, major). One pre-existing gap deferred: exportChat silently no-ops with no user feedback when currentChat is falsy (unchanged guard, out of this change's scope). Seven candidates dismissed as noise: an unreachable unhandled-rejection claim (downloadFileStream never rejects), a functionally-redundant but harmless branch, a latent aria-label fallback bug never triggered because every current call site (old and new) supplies or resolves a safe label, the by-design/spec-confirmed drop of includeToolOutputs for non-docx/pdf formats, a trivial untested explicit-false case that is provably equivalent to the tested undefined case, a well-justified jsdom OverlayPanel test mock, and an unmount-during-export race that produces no observable consequence on React 19. All four lenses ran with parseable output, standards audit completed with no coverage gap, and no decision_needed items remain.

findings.title: Export filename ignores tool-outputs variant
findings.problem: exportChat builds the download filename as `${name}.${format}` regardless of includeToolOutputs, so a with-tool-outputs export and a default export of the same conversation and format resolve to the identical filename.
findings.impact: A user who downloads both variants in one session gets indistinguishable files on disk (browser auto-rename or overwrite), defeating the point of offering the two variants this change introduces.
findings.recommendation: Append a suffix (e.g. `_with_tool_outputs`) to `name` when includeToolOutputs is true, before building the filename passed to api.downloadFileStream.
